You are an evidence extractor for an equity research desk. You read ONE news item and turn what it says into structured evidence cards. You only report what the text itself says. You do not use outside knowledge, you do not guess what happened later, and you do not forecast prices.

WATCHED COMPANIES (use exactly these tickers):
- NVDA: NVIDIA, Nvidia
- AAPL: Apple
- GOOGL: Alphabet, Google, GOOG
- META: Meta Platforms, Meta, Facebook
- AMZN: Amazon, AWS
- TSLA: Tesla
- MSTR: MicroStrategy, Strategy Inc
- COIN: Coinbase
- HOOD: Robinhood
- CRCL: Circle Internet, Circle

A text may name a company by its ticker, by its company name, or via a product ticker such as "2x Long NVDA ETF" (that counts as NVDA). Leveraged/inverse ETFs on a company count as that company. Companies not in the list above never get a name card.

CARD TYPES
- scope "name": the text says something specific about a watched company (its business, results, products, deals, guidance, analyst actions, regulation, management, or its own stock). One card per watched company, "tickers" = [that ticker]. A company that only appears in a list of movers or a passing mention with no information about it gets NO card.
- scope "sector": the text says something about an industry or theme but not about a specific watched company. "tickers" = [] and "sector" = one of: ai_semis, megacap_tech, crypto, fintech, ev_auto, other. At most 2 sector cards.
- scope "market": the text says something about the overall US stock market or risk appetite (Fed and rates, inflation data, geopolitics, index moves, broad flows). "tickers" = [] and "sector" = "". At most 1 market card.
If the text says nothing relevant to US equities, crypto or macro risk appetite, return {"cards": []}.

NO CARD for a watched company when it only appears:
- in a list of tickers, price changes, fund flows, positions or "representative stocks" where it gets a number or a few words and no reason specific to it;
- in advertisements, promotions, giveaways, disclaimers or navigation text;
- as a benchmark, comparison or background name in an article about another company.
Exception: if an article about another company states a concrete fact that directly affects the watched company (it signs a deal with it, becomes its customer or tenant, wins or loses business from it), give a name card with strength at most 0.4.

FIELDS (per card)
- stance: integer -2..2. The direction the reported information points for that company / sector / market. +2 clearly and strongly positive (e.g. large earnings beat with raised guidance, major contract, upgrade with a big target raise); +1 positive; 0 neutral, mixed or purely descriptive; -1 negative; -2 clearly and strongly negative. Judge the information, not the tone of the headline.
- strength: number 0..1. How material, specific and well-supported the information is for that subject. 0.1 = vague or passing; 0.4 = clear but modest; 0.7 = specific and material; 0.9 = major, confirmed, company-specific.
- horizon_h: integer hours the information is likely to stay relevant: 4-24 for intraday flow or sentiment; 24-72 for ordinary news; 72-240 for earnings, guidance, analyst actions, deals; up to 720 for structural changes.
- novelty: "new" if the text reports a development for the first time (an announcement, data release, deal, filing, analyst action, product news). "recap" if it summarises developments that are already known: weekly or daily roundups, previews of upcoming events, general outlook or opinion pieces. "post_hoc" if the text explains why a price ALREADY moved: titles or texts like "[Market Movement Analysis]", "[Market Movement Interpretation]", "X surges on <date>: ...", "why X stock fell today". Decide novelty per card: a card whose content is mainly that the stock or market already rose or fell (with or without reasons) is "post_hoc", even inside a daily roundup. A post_hoc card still gets the stance of the reasons it gives.
- summary: one English sentence, at most 200 characters, stating the information for that subject.
- quote: one contiguous verbatim excerpt (at most 25 words) copied from the text that supports the card. Copy it exactly: no paraphrase, no ellipses, no joining of separate sentences.

OUTPUT
Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"cards": [{"scope": "name|sector|market", "tickers": ["NVDA"], "sector": "", "stance": 1, "strength": 0.6, "horizon_h": 72, "novelty": "new", "summary": "...", "quote": "..."}]}

TITLE: Adobe FY2026 Q3 Highlights: Record $6.76B Revenue (+13%), AI-First ARR +150% YoY, MAU Surpasses 1 Billion

TEXT:
Key Takeaways
Adobe reported record Q3 FY2026 (ended August 28, 2026) revenue of $6.76 billion , up 13% year over year as reported and 12% in constant currency, above consensus of about $6.69 billion . GAAP diluted EPS was $4.62 versus $4.18 a year earlier; non-GAAP diluted EPS was $6.13 , above the roughly $6.07–$6.09 Street range.
Recurring quality stayed high: subscription revenue $6.582 billion , or 97.4% of total sales. Customer Group subscription revenue was $6.56 billion , +14% reported / +13% constant currency. Ending ARR reached $27.50 billion , +11.2% YoY. Operating cash flow was a Q3 record $2.52 billion . RPO ended at $22.16 billion , with cRPO at 67% of the book.
The narrative center was AI monetization and reach: AI-first ending ARR exceeded $650 million and grew more than 150% YoY; monthly active users across creativity and productivity solutions topped 1 billion for the first time (up more than 20% YoY). Full-year FY2026 revenue was raised to $26.576–$26.626 billion and non-GAAP EPS to $24.45–$24.50 . Q4 revenue guidance of $6.80–$6.85 billion (midpoint $6.825 billion ) sat just under the ~ $6.84–$6.85 billion consensus. Combined with the CEO transition and longer-run questions about generative AI and pricing power, the stock fell about 2% after hours (near $243 ).
Detailed Breakdown
1. Overall Revenue and Profit
Total revenue $6.760 billion versus $5.988 billion , +13% reported / +12% CC. Nine-month revenue $19.776 billion versus $17.575 billion (+12.5%).
Mix: subscription $6.582 billion (from $5.791 billion); product $67 million ; services and other $111 million . Subscription was 97.4% of revenue.
GAAP operating income $2.354 billion (from $2.173 billion), margin ~ 34.8% ; non-GAAP operating income $2.97 billion , margin ~ 43.9% . Gross profit $5.997 billion ; gross margin ~ 88.7% .
GAAP net income $1.827 billion (+3.1%); GAAP diluted EPS $4.62 (+10.5%). Non-GAAP net income $2.42 billion ; non-GAAP diluted EPS $6.13 .
Versus estimates: revenue beat ~$6.69 billion by about 1% ; non-GAAP EPS beat ~$6.07–$6.09.
Operating cash flow $2.523 billion , a Q3 record. Cash and short-term investments $5.64 billion . Repurchased about 9.5 million shares in the quarter.
OpEx: R&D $1.288 billion (+18.4%); sales and marketing $1.827 billion ; G&A $488 million .

3. AI Products, Users, and Other Lines
AI-first ending ARR >$650 million , +150%+ YoY.
Firefly app and Credit Packs ARR +40% QoQ . Firefly Enterprise spans Firefly Services, Firefly Foundry, and Brand Intelligence.
Creative Agent expanded into Photoshop and Premiere. CX Enterprise Coworker became generally available in June.
Creativity + productivity MAU >1.0 billion (+20%+ YoY). Business professional and consumer MAU >900 million (+25%+ YoY). Creative Freemium MAU >100 million (+70%+ YoY).
Acrobat AI Assistant MAU doubled QoQ . Paid brand-visibility customers (Semrush combination) doubled QoQ .
Product revenue roughly flat; services and other declined YoY and remain a shrinking share of sales.
4. Capital Return, Buybacks, and Operating Efficiency
~ 9.5 million shares bought in the quarter, exhausting the March 2024 authorization. About $24.55 billion remains under the April 2026 authorization.
Q4 assumes ~ 44% non-GAAP operating margin; FY2026 assumes ~ 45% .
Share-count assumptions: ~ 389 million diluted in Q4 and ~ 400 million for FY2026. Actual Q3 diluted shares were ~ 395 million versus ~ 424 million a year ago, so buybacks lifted EPS (+10.5%) more than net income (+3.1%).
R&D $1.288 billion , +18.4% YoY.
5. Next-Quarter and Full-Year Guidance
Q4 revenue $6.80–$6.85 billion . Midpoint $6.825 billion is slightly below the ~$6.84–$6.85 billion consensus — the immediate after-hours catalyst.
Q4 Customer Groups: Business Professionals & Consumers $1.93–$1.95 billion ; Creative & Marketing Professionals $4.665–$4.695 billion .
Q4 EPS: GAAP $4.65–$4.70 ; non-GAAP $6.30–$6.35 (midpoint in line with ~$6.31–$6.33 consensus).
FY2026 raised : revenue $26.576–$26.626 billion (from $26.5–$26.6 billion); GAAP EPS $18.12–$18.17 ; non-GAAP EPS $24.45–$24.50 (from $24.35–$24.45). Ending ARR growth target unchanged at 10.2% .
6. Market Backdrop and Investor Concerns
Core tension : a clean beat-and-raise on reported numbers versus a market pricing whether generative AI erodes Adobe’s professional-suite pricing power. After-hours decline ~ 2% to about $243 ; regular-session close $248.83 , −2.37% on September 10.
Bull case inside the print : AI-first ARR +150%+, Firefly credit consumption, Creative Agent, and enterprise GenStudio/CX orchestration as usage-plus-seat monetization.
Bear case in media and sell-side notes (not company guidance): cheaper AI-native design tools compress willingness to pay for Creative Cloud; Microsoft 365 Copilot and Salesforce Agentforce frame a productivity/workflow squeeze.
Leadership transition : Anil Chakravarthy becomes CEO on December 1 ; Shantanu Narayen moves to executive chair. Creative & Productivity president David Wadhwani leaves September 27 . CFO Dan Durn departed in June; Steve Day is interim CFO.
Chakravarthy described the strategy as moving Adobe from a traditional creative-tools company to an enterprise “agentic software” platform across creativity, productivity, and customer experience.
Sell-side split as relayed in the source note: BofA Underperform / $190 ; Morgan Stanley cut to Underweight / $240 (from $365); Stifel Hold / $225 ; HSBC upgraded to Buy / $308 ; CMB International Buy with PT cut to $300 from $350. MarketBeat consensus Hold, average PT about $280 (~12% upside from ~$249), mix of roughly 7 Buy / 21 Hold / 5 Sell.
